title: Yet Heard

location.name: The phone-booth sidewalk below the club, Atlantis
location.kind: night city sidewalk with a lit phone booth, opening by phone onto a Baltimere living room and the Inner Harbor
location.real_analog: A Centro Histórico, Mexico City sidewalk at night with a street payphone booth (inferred from the Mexico City motorcycle source note at this poem's end); for the father walk, the Baltimore Inner Harbor promenade and piers before dawn
near: the Dance & Self rooftop club overhead (Newly Single)
an Atlantis street running toward the moon
the parked motorcycle at the curb (Magic Ride)
by phone: mother's living room in Baltimere (map HOME (URBAN) / WINDOW)
by phone: the Inner Harbor, quiet docks and pier lights in Baltimere

situation: Walking out of the club, the POET sees the EX in the sidewalk crowd (back only, no face) and cannot reach him; then the two walk an Atlantis street together, talking, the moon in the distance. They end up on the sidewalk by a phone booth with suitcases at their feet. The POET calls his MOTHER, who watches the break-up from the booth and then from her living room; he calls his FATHER, who appears and walks with him east along paths toward the sunrise and the inner harbor, the break-up always continuing in the background. Back on the sidewalk, the EX turns to haze and disappears.
time_of_day: late night, moon up; the father walk heads toward a pre-dawn sunrise
weather_light: moonlight down the street, neon and booth glow, wet pavement with moon reflections in puddles (spine YH010; rain inferred from the Juice Jones 'The Rain' inspo), harbor moonlight on ripples

set_pieces.name: The EX in the crowd
set_pieces.what_happens: Leaving the club amid fawning crowds, the POET glimpses the EX from behind and reaches for him but cannot get through.
set_pieces.camera: handheld follow through the crowd; EX kept back-to-camera, soft focus, reaching hand in foreground

set_pieces.name: Walking toward the moon
set_pieces.what_happens: POET and EX walk down the Atlantis street together, talking, the moon at the end of the street; they 'grow old together' in feeling only (aging not literal).
lines: the way we used to see it
set_pieces.camera: long tracking two-shot from behind (EX's face never shown), moon framed at the vanishing point; insert of both reflections in a puddle
set_pieces.position: along the street, heading toward the moon

set_pieces.name: Suitcases at the phone booth
set_pieces.what_happens: EX and POET stand on the sidewalk near the phone booth with suitcases at their feet; the EX helps him pack to go.
set_pieces.camera: low shot at suitcase level, booth light spilling on the curb; EX present only as hands and back

set_pieces.name: The call to Mother
set_pieces.what_happens: POET enters the booth and calls his MOTHER; they talk while watching the POET and EX break up on the sidewalk; cut to POET and MOTHER in her living room, the break-up still in the background. He hangs up and she disappears.
set_pieces.camera: through the booth glass with the break-up on the sidewalk behind; in the living room, a window frame holding the sidewalk scene (window inferred)
set_pieces.position: inside the phone booth, then mother's living room (Baltimere home)

set_pieces.name: Father and son to the inner harbor
set_pieces.what_happens: POET calls his FATHER, who appears from the yonders and watches the break-up; they walk paths east toward the sunrise and stroll the inner harbor, the break-up continuing in the background.
set_pieces.camera: wide walking shot along pier lights from behind, dawn ahead; break-up layered in the background plate
set_pieces.position: paths running east from the booth to the harbor promenade and piers

set_pieces.name: The EX turns to haze
set_pieces.what_happens: POET and EX are back on the sidewalk; the EX turns to haze and disappears, leaving the POET alone.
set_pieces.camera: locked-off wide two-shot; the EX dissolves out, hold on the POET alone at the curb

arrival.from_previous: He leaves the rooftop club and walks down the street below; crowds on the sidewalk fawn over him (no voice-over).

departure.to_next: He does not travel: the EX turns to haze on the sidewalk, and the POET is left alone on the same sidewalk beside a parked motorcycle where Magic Ride opens.

motifs: the moon 'the way we used to'
the break-up looping in the background
encoding: The sidewalk is the hinge between the club's escape and the ride out: a public, in-between place where a private break-up must play out with everyone (and both parents) watching. The phone booth works as a portal from Atlantis back to Baltimere, the zone the map glosses as 'sea-edge memories, personal origins'; inferred: calling home collapses the distance so mother and father can witness. The EX can only dissolve here, at the curb, because this is where the luggage stands and leaving begins.

open_questions: Is the father's harbor walk a literal journey to Baltimere/Baltimore's Inner Harbor, or a summoned vision on the Atlantis street? The map's YET HEARD node sits in Atlantis while its harbor landmarks sit in the Baltimere corner.
Does the living room show the sidewalk through a window, or is the break-up composited in? (window inferred)
Treatment: 'POET calls MOTHER (enters phonebooth?)' — booth entry itself is marked uncertain.
Is it raining? Only the Juice Jones 'The Rain' inspo and the spine's puddle support wet streets.
